questions.q_en: Nobody in the department was willing to accept responsibility for the lapse, ______?
questions.q_hi: Nobody in the department was willing to accept responsibility for the lapse, ______?
options_en: were they
was he
did they
wasn’t he
options_hi: were they
was he
did they
wasn’t he
questions.solution_en:
👉 The correct answer is - “were they”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Indefinite Pronoun + Auxiliary Repetition Rule

Words like nobody, no one, none make a sentence negative in meaning. When the statement is negative → the tag must be positive.

Also, when the main clause already contains an auxiliary verb (is/was/were/has/have etc.), we must repeat the same auxiliary in the tag.

For indefinite pronouns referring to persons, the tag pronoun is they.

💢 Application to the Given Question

Nobody in the department was willing to accept responsibility for the lapse

  • “Nobody” → negative meaning

  • So, the tag must be positive

  • The auxiliary used in the main clause is was

  • Since the pronoun in the tag is they, the auxiliary changes to were

Therefore: were they?

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ - Nobody was present at the venue, were they?

Example 2 ✅ - No one was prepared for the inspection, were they?

Example 3 ✅ - None of the employees was informed earlier, were they?

🧠 Things to Remember

If auxiliary is already present → repeat it in the tag.

  • Nobody / No one → use “they” in tag.

  • Negative meaning → positive tag.

  • Avoid unnecessary do-support.

questions.q_en:
Identify the type of the highlighted non-finite phrase.

The committee appointed a special team to investigate the financial irregularities reported during the audit.
questions.q_hi:
Identify the type of the highlighted non-finite phrase.

The committee appointed a special team to investigate the financial irregularities reported during the audit.
questions.solution_en:
Answer: D) Infinitive Phrase

Explanation: An infinitive phrase begins with “to + base verb” and may function as a noun, adjective, or adverb.

The highlighted phrase begins with:

“to investigate”

Hence, it is an infinitive phrase. Here, it functions as an adjective because it describes the purpose of the “special team.”

Which team? → team to investigate the financial irregularities

Why other options are incorrect:

A) A gerund phrase begins with an -ing form acting as a noun.

B) A participial phrase begins with a participle (-ing/-ed form).

C) A noun phrase functions purely as a noun and is not built around “to + verb.”

questions.q_en:
Select the passive form of the given sentence:

"The acquisition deal offered the shareholders a 20% premium over the market price."
questions.q_hi:
Select the passive form of the given sentence:

"The acquisition deal offered the shareholders a 20% premium over the market price."
options_en: The shareholders were offered a 20% premium over the market price.
A 20% premium was offered to the shareholders over the market price.
A 20% premium was offered the shareholders over the market price.
Both (A) and (B) are correct.
options_hi: The shareholders were offered a 20% premium over the market price.
A 20% premium was offered to the shareholders over the market price.
A 20% premium was offered the shareholders over the market price.
Both (A) and (B) are correct.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (D)

📌 Rule / Concept: Double Object Verbs – Active to Passive Conversion
When a verb takes two objects (Indirect Object + Direct Object), the passive can be formed in two ways: (1) Indirect object as subject → Indirect Object + was/were + V³ + Direct Object. (2) Direct object as subject → Direct Object + was/were + V³ + to + Indirect Object. The tense must remain unchanged during conversion.

📌 Application to the Given Question

The acquisition deal offered the shareholders a 20% premium over the market price. Here, “offered” is in the simple past tense and takes two objects: “the shareholders” (indirect object) and “a 20% premium” (direct object). Passive Form 1: “The shareholders were offered a 20% premium over the market price.” Passive Form 2: “A 20% premium was offered to the shareholders over the market price.” Both structures are grammatically correct. Option (C) omits the required preposition “to” when the direct object becomes the subject, making it incorrect.

💡 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Verbs like give, offer, send, teach allow two passive forms. If the direct object becomes the subject, use “to” (or “for,” depending on the verb). Maintain the original tense. Check whether both options are grammatically correct before selecting one.

A sudden __________ the weather patterns forced the captain to __________ his route, though he refused to __________ his ship __________ a faster vessel despite the approaching storm.

options_en: change in / change / change for

change of / change / change with
change in / change in / change for

questions.solution_en:
Rule / Concept: Change as Verb vs. Noun

The word "change" follows specific prepositional rules based on its part of speech and context:

Application to the Given Question

"A sudden change in the weather patterns forced the captain to change his route, though he refused to change his ship for a faster vessel..."

First Blank: "Change" is a noun here followed by "weather patterns" (an alteration in state), requiring "in".

Second Blank: "Change" is a verb followed by the object "his route." Since it's a direct alteration, no preposition is needed.

Third Blank: "Change... for" is used because the captain is being asked to replace/exchange his current ship with a different one.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

questions.q_en: He is ______ brave a soldier that everyone respects him.
questions.q_hi: He is ______ brave a soldier that everyone respects him.
options_en: Any of the above
options_hi: Any of the above
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option C

👉 Replace the blank with “so”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Degree Modifiers – So vs. Such with Noun Phrases

In formal English grammar, both "so" and "such" can be used to emphasize an adjective that leads to a consequence (expressed by the "that" clause). However, the placement of the indefinite article (a/an) determines which modifier is grammatically correct.

Structure 1: So + Adjective + a/an + Singular Countable Noun + that...

Example: It was so boring a movie that I fell asleep halfway through.

Structure 2: Such + a/an + Adjective + Noun + that...

Example: It was such a boring movie that I fell asleep halfway through.

The word "very" always precedes the entire noun phrase.

Correct: A very brave soldier.

✅ Corrected Sentence

He is so brave a soldier that everyone respects him.

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1: It was so fine a day that we went for a picnic.

Example 2: She is such a talented singer that she won the national award.

No sooner did the bell ring ____ the students left the classroom.
questions.q_hi:
The following sentence contains a blank space, followed by four alternative options. You are required to choose the most appropriate option (A, B, C, or D) that grammatically completes the sentence in accordance with the rules of English grammar.

No sooner did the bell ring ____ the students left the classroom.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option C

👉 Replace the blank with “than”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Correlative Adverbs (No sooner... than)

In English grammar, the phrasal conjunction “No sooner” is used to show that one action took place immediately after another. It is a strict grammatical rule that “No sooner” must always be followed by the conjunction “than”.

Structure: No sooner + Auxiliary Verb (did/had) + Subject + Main Verb ... than + Subject + Second Action.

Inversion: When a sentence begins with a negative expression like "No sooner," the auxiliary verb must precede the subject (Inversion).

Corrected Sentence: No sooner did the bell ring than the students left the classroom.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

He got so angry during the debate that he was completely __________ by his emotions.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

He got so angry during the debate that he was completely __________ by his emotions.
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (1).

English Explanation: “Carry away” (usually used as “carried away”) means to lose control because of strong emotions such as anger, excitement, or enthusiasm. In the sentence, he became so angry during the debate that he lost control of his emotions. Therefore, “carried away” correctly conveys the idea of being overwhelmed by feelings. “Carry out” means to execute or complete a task. “Carry on” means to continue something. “Carry off” means to succeed in doing something difficult or to win something. Since the context refers to losing emotional control, “carried away” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Carried away (भावनाओं में बह जाना / बहक जाना)
Example: He was carried away by excitement after seeing his name in the merit list. (मेरिट सूची में अपना नाम देखकर वह उत्साह में बह गया।)

2. Carried out (पूरा करना / कार्यान्वित करना)
Example: The police carried out a detailed investigation. (पुलिस ने विस्तृत जांच की।)

3. Carried on (जारी रखना)
Example: Despite the noise, she carried on with her studies. (शोर के बावजूद उसने पढ़ाई जारी रखी।)

4. Carried off (सफलतापूर्वक कर लेना / जीत लेना)
Example: She carried off the award for best performer. (उसने सर्वश्रेष्ठ प्रदर्शन का पुरस्कार जीत लिया।)

questions.q_en:
Efforts to promote social justice often involve addressing deeply rooted inequalities that have persisted across generations. While policy interventions aim to ensure equal opportunity, critics argue that superficial reforms may [---1---] existing power structures rather than dismantle them. Moreover, initiatives that ignore social context risk being perceived as [---2---], offering symbolic reassurance without producing material change. Marginalized communities, having experienced repeated cycles of unmet promises, frequently respond with [---3---] skepticism toward institutional narratives of inclusion. Sustainable progress therefore demands a [---4---] commitment to equity—one that confronts systemic barriers instead of merely alleviating their visible symptoms.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [4] :
questions.q_hi:
Efforts to promote social justice often involve addressing deeply rooted inequalities that have persisted across generations. While policy interventions aim to ensure equal opportunity, critics argue that superficial reforms may [---1---] existing power structures rather than dismantle them. Moreover, initiatives that ignore social context risk being perceived as [---2---], offering symbolic reassurance without producing material change. Marginalized communities, having experienced repeated cycles of unmet promises, frequently respond with [---3---] skepticism toward institutional narratives of inclusion. Sustainable progress therefore demands a [---4---] commitment to equity—one that confronts systemic barriers instead of merely alleviating their visible symptoms.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in the blank [4] :
options_en: cosmetic
tentative
calibrated
substantive
options_hi: cosmetic
tentative
calibrated
substantive
questions.solution_en:
Substantive refers to deep, meaningful, and structural change. The passage argues for confronting systemic barriers rather than surface symptoms, making substantive commitment the most contextually sound choice.
WHY OTHER OPTIONS ARE WRONG
• Cosmetic refers to surface-level change, explicitly criticized.
• Tentative suggests uncertainty or lack of resolve.
• Calibrated implies balance, but the emphasis here is on depth and seriousness.

questions.solution_en:
Rule / Concept: (Angry/Annoyed/Vexed/Disgusted – At vs. With)

In competitive grammar, specific prepositions are used to indicate the target of these emotions:

Application to the Given Question

"...visibly annoyed at the blatant inconsistencies... but he remained... annoyed with the junior accountant..."

In the first part of the sentence, the auditor is reacting to "inconsistencies" (a thing/situation), which requires "at". In the second part, the target of the emotion is the "junior accountant" (a person), which requires "with". The original sentence flipped these, making it grammatically incorrect.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: I never remember to
have seen a more dedicated
teacher in my entire life.
No error
options_hi: I never remember to
have seen a more dedicated
teacher in my entire life.
No error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A)

Replace “I never remember” with “I do not remember ever” (or "I remember never")

Rule / Concept: Placement of "Never" with "Remember"

The word "never" is an adverb of frequency. In English grammar, its placement changes the meaning of the sentence significantly:

  1. I never remember: This implies that the act of remembering has never happened in your life (which is illogical, as you are currently trying to recall a memory).

  2. I remember never / I do not remember ever: This implies that you have a memory of many things, but "seeing a dedicated teacher" is not among them

application to the Given Question

The sentence intends to say that in all of the speaker's past experiences, they haven't seen someone so dedicated.

  • The Logic Error: If you say "I never remember," it sounds like you have a permanent case of amnesia. You aren't saying that you never perform the action of remembering; you are saying that in your memory, this event has not occurred.

  • The Fix: Shift the negative emphasis. You do remember your life, but you don't remember ever seeing such a teacher.

Corrected Sentence

I do not remember ever to have seen a more dedicated teacher in my entire life. (Alternatively: I remember never to have seen...)

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The sick admitted in the hospital are receiving
timely treatment, but some sick has not been
attended properly due to shortage of staff.
options_hi: The sick admitted in the hospital are receiving
timely treatment, but some sick has not been
attended properly due to shortage of staff.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option B.

Replace "has" with "have".

Rule/Concept: Nouns that look like adjectives (Adjective-like Nouns)

Some words like sick, poor, rich, young, blind are Nouns even though they often describe a group like adjectives. When they are plural in meaning or refer to multiple people, the verb must agree with the plural sense.

Application to the Given Question: "but some sick has not been attended properly due to shortage of staff."

Here, some sick refers to multiple patients, so the verb must be plural → "have" instead of "has".

Corrected Sentence: but some sick have not been attended properly due to shortage of staff.

More Examples for Clarity:

The poor have been given relief during the flood.

The blind are often ignored in public transport.

The young aspire to excel in competitive exams.

Incorrect Usage:

The rich has donated money for charity.

The sick was waiting for hours in the hospital.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips:

Always identify if the word is acting as a Noun (even if it looks like an Adjective).

Check subject-verb agreement carefully; plural sense → plural verb.

In SSC CGL, this is a common trap in Spot the Error questions.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The revolutionary theories proposed by Adam Smith
have shaped the fundamental principles of modern
economic thought in the eighteenth century.
No Error
options_hi: The revolutionary theories proposed by Adam Smith
have shaped the fundamental principles of modern
economic thought in the eighteenth century.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “have shaped” with “shaped”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Simple Past vs. Present Perfect with Specific Time Markers -

The Present Perfect Tense (has/have + V3) is used for actions that happened at an unspecific time or have a direct connection to the present. However, as soon as a specific past time marker (like yesterday, in 1947, in the 18th century, ago) is mentioned, the action is "anchored" in the past and disconnected from the present. In such cases, you must use the Simple Past Tense (V2).

💢 Application to the Given Question - The phrase "in the eighteenth century" is a specific, finished period of time. It acts as a "dead" time marker. Because the sentence specifies exactly when this shaping occurred (a time that is now over), the Present Perfect "have shaped" is grammatically incorrect. It must be changed to the Simple Past "shaped" to match the finished time reference.

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1: I bought this car in 2015. (Specific year = Simple Past) ✅

Example 2: The Egyptian civilization flourished thousands of years ago. ("Ago" = Simple Past) ✅

Example 3: We have studied these theories. (No specific time = Present Perfect is okay) ✅

📌 Rule / Concept: The Present Subjunctive Mood (Imperative Adjectives)

The Present Subjunctive is used in "that-clauses" following adjectives that express necessity, urgency, or importance (e.g., imperative, essential, vital, crucial, necessary). In this formal mood, the verb in the "that-clause" must be in its base form (the infinitive without "to"), even if the subject is third-person singular (he, she, it, or a singular noun).

💢 Application to the Given Question - The adjective imperative acts as the trigger. The subject of the following clause is "the envoy" (singular). While standard grammar would require "meets," the subjunctive mood demands the base form meet.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The recent statistics clearly __________ the researcher’s hypothesis about rising inflation.
questions.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank.

The recent statistics clearly __________ the researcher’s hypothesis about rising inflation.
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (3).

English Explanation: “Bear out” means to confirm, support, or prove that something is true, usually with evidence or facts. In the sentence, the recent statistics are supporting or proving the researcher’s hypothesis about rising inflation. Therefore, “bear out” correctly conveys the idea of confirming a claim with evidence. “Bear up” means to remain strong during difficulty. “Bear down” means to apply pressure or concentrate intensely. “Bear with” means to be patient with someone. Since the context refers to evidence confirming a hypothesis, “bear out” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Bear up (हिम्मत बनाए रखना)
Meaning in Hindi: कठिन परिस्थितियों में मजबूत बने रहना।
Example: She bore up well despite the challenges. (चुनौतियों के बावजूद उसने हिम्मत बनाए रखी।)

2. Bear down (दबाव डालना / ज़ोर लगाना)
Meaning in Hindi: पूरी ताकत लगाना या दबाव बनाना।
Example: The lawyer bore down on the witness with tough questions. (वकील ने गवाह पर कठिन प्रश्नों के साथ दबाव डाला।)

3. Bear out (पुष्टि करना / सही साबित करना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी दावे या कथन की पुष्टि करना।
Example 1: The data collected from the survey bears out the claim that unemployment has increased. (सर्वे से एकत्रित आँकड़े इस दावे की पुष्टि करते हैं कि बेरोज़गारी बढ़ी है।)
Example 2: The results bore out his prediction. (परिणामों ने उसकी भविष्यवाणी को सही साबित किया।)

4. Bear with (धैर्य रखना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी के साथ धैर्य रखना या प्रतीक्षा करना।
Example: Please bear with me while I fix this issue. (कृपया इस समस्या को ठीक करते समय धैर्य रखें।)
